name: Iterative 3D Super-Resolution
definition: A two-stage alternating training process for super-resolving NeRFs. Stage 1 (Upscaling) uses RSD to upscale 2D NeRF renders into high-resolution, LR-consistent images. Stage 2 (Synchronization) updates the NeRF parameters using these upscaled images as training inputs to capture view-consistent 3D details.
summary: Iterative 3D Super-Resolution is a two-stage framework that super-resolves NeRFs by alternating diffusion-based upscaling with synchronization to enforce multi-view consistency and reduce optimization time.
